transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-11-25
Start time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 62 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Kline (Redwood AE), Priya Menon (Redwood SE), Evan Torres (Redwood Platform), Dr. Maya Redd (CTO, Sable Pharma), Liam Chen (SRE), Aisha Patel (ML Engineer), Tom Ruiz (Product)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be incomplete):
- Deep dive on mapping Redwood runtime events to OpenTelemetry spans and metrics; focus on token-level visibility for debugging hallucinations and cost accounting.
- Discussed sampling strategies, span/metric attributes to add (model_id, seq_len, kv_cache_hit, batch_size), and dashboards for p50/p95 token latency and cost per 1k tokens.
- Agreed next steps: share OTel attr/metrics list, SOW for 3-week dedicated pilot, customer to provide test prompt corpus and staging access.

Topics: OpenTelemetry, token-level metrics, KV cache, batching, quantization, VPC visibility, dashboards, OTLP/Prometheus/Grafana

Transcript body:
[00:00] Jordan (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro? we'll make this a hands-on session, Priya will drive the runtime/tracing parts.
[00:18] Dr. Maya Redd (Sable): Hi all — thanks. we're trying to get better visibility into per-token latency and cache behavior in our inference pipeline, especially once we move some models on-prem.
[00:30] Priya (Redwood SE): Great. quick agenda: 1) how we emit token-level events and translate to OTel spans/metrics; 2) what to surface in Grafana dashboards; 3) sampling & cost; 4) VPC/on-prem considerations.
[00:45] Liam (SRE): sounds good. we use an OTLP collector -> prometheus -> grafana already in production. prefer not to introduce a bunch of custom exporters.
[01:02] Priya: that's fine — we'll show how the Redwood runtime can export OTLP traces and metrics natively or via our OTLP bridge. we also emit structured logs for traces correlation.
[01:20] Aisha (ML Eng): one big ask: we need to know whether a token came from KV cache or from model decode, right? we want to attribute cost and quality.
[01:32] Evan (Redwood Platform): right — we add a "kv.cache_hit" attribute on relevant spans and an aggregate metric kv_cache_hits_total with labels model_id, customer_id, seq_len_bucket.
[01:45] Speaker 1: (mumble) sometimes the attribute names are a bit different in our exporter...
[01:58] Priya: yeah, apologies for the quick patch names in earlier docs; we'll send a canonical list. recommended span attributes: model.id, model.variant, request.id, seq_len, tokens_generated, kv.cache_hit (boolean), batch.size, routing.policy, quantization.profile.
[02:25] Tom (Product): how heavy is emitting per-token spans? concerns about overhead.
[02:37] Priya: good question — we don't create a full OTel span per token by default because that is expensive. pattern is: per-request parent span, and then lightweight "token events" as span events or metric increments. for deep debugging you can enable per-token spans but with sampling.
[02:58] Liam: that matches our instinct. do you provide an OTLP histogram for token latencies? we rely on histograms for percentiles.
[03:12] Evan: yes — we export token_latency_seconds histogram buckets and token_count per request. p50/p95/p99 are available from Prometheus. also provide derived_metrics like cost_per_1k_tokens label'd by model and quantization_profile.
[03:34] Dr. Maya: can we see a real example?
[03:40] Priya: sure — sharing my screen (link: redwood/otl-demo-2025-11-25.png). example trace: parent span "redwood.inference.request" (attributes: model.id=rw-llama-13b, seq_len=256, batch.size=1) with events: [token_emit (t=35ms, token_idx=1), token_emit (t=72ms, token_idx=2) ...]. attribute kv.cache_hit=true set on event when prefix retrieved from cache.
[04:12] Aisha: what's the storage cost of token events if we keep them for 30 days?
[04:20] Priya: token events are small but numerous. our recommendation: keep aggregated metrics (kv cache hit rate, token latency histograms) for 30+ days, and store sampled traces (1-5%) for 90 days depending on compliance. we can wire to your existing object store or to our retention tier.
[04:42] Liam: about batching — we do a lot of batching to reduce costs; how do you attach token-level timings when multiple sequences share the same decoder step?
[04:55] Evan: when batching, we annotate per-example offsets within the batch. request span contains batch.size and we emit per-example subspan events with token indices and per-token timings. important to add attribute batch.index so you can correlate token timing to specific conversation.
[05:18] Jordan: and note the effect: batching increases throughput but shifts tail latency; the P95 may rise if one long sequence is in batch. we recommend affinity rules in Dedicated mode to keep similar seq_len together to avoid head-of-line blocking.
[05:40] Tom: ok — quantization then. we have a compliance/regulatory requirement to run on-prem for some workloads; we may use 4-bit quantized models. any observability caveats?
[05:54] Priya: quantization profiles should be tagged as quant.profile in the span. quantized models may have smaller variance in latency but sometimes higher decode jitter depending on kernel implementation. also, some hardware doesn't expose fine-grained kernel timings; in those cases we fallback to host-side timing instrumentation which we surface as estimate_token_kernel_ms attribute.
[06:20] Dr. Maya: VPC/on-prem: our security team needs to see OTLP traffic routing and assurance that trace data does not leak across customers.
[06:34] Evan: in Private we provide a local collector inside your VPC. OTLP data stays inside the VPC; we support mTLS for the collector and integration with your KMS for key management. we also support per-customer telemetry namespaces so metrics are labeled with customer_id but never aggregated across tenants in a single metric stream unless you opt-in.
[06:58] Liam: do you support sampling rules based on error rate or on model id? we'd like to sample more when hallucination rate rises.
[07:12] Priya: yes — sampling can be dynamic. Redwood exposes a control API to instruct the runtime to increase span sampling for selected model.id or when token-level quality metrics (we emit a synth_metric 'suspect_token_rate') exceed a threshold. You can tie rules to alerts in Prometheus.
[07:38] Aisha: about token-level quality metrics — how do you compute suspect_token_rate?
[07:45] Priya: it's an example synthetic metric: we run lightweight heuristics at decode time (n-gram repetition, low softmax entropy, plugin-based checks) and emit an event token_suspect=true. upstream can ingest these and build suspect_token_rate as ratio over tokens_generated. it's configurable and can be enriched by your eval labels.
[08:10] Speaker 2: (background noise)
[08:20] Jordan: we should run a short demo of how this looks in Grafana — Evan, do you have the staging dashboard link?
[08:28] Evan: sharing (link: grafana.sandbox.sablepharma.internal/d/okR2S-token-trace). Dashboard panels: token_latency (histogram), kv_cache_hit_rate, batch_size_dist, cost_per_1k_tokens, suspect_token_rate heatmap by model.variant.
[08:52] Tom: the cost_per_1k looks useful for finance. how accurate is it with prefix caching?
[09:02] Priya: cost includes decoded tokens only minus cached prefix tokens when kv_cache_hit=true; we compute both gross_token_count and billable_token_count. there's also a metric cached_prefix_tokens_total.
[09:20] Dr. Maya: we want to map trace ids back to request ids in our app logs. is there an easy way?
[09:29] Evan: yes, we propagate traceparent header and include request.id as a trace attribute; we also add a short request_tag you can index. If you use our SDK, the correlation is automatic. If you use OTLP, ensure your collector keeps trace->log coupling by forwarding trace id to log pipeline.
[09:50] Liam: latency targets: our SLA target is p95 <= 350ms for interactive assistant. how does batching affect that?
[10:02] Priya: batching helps throughput, but for strict p95 latency you want smaller batch sizes or dedicated pools with reserved capacity. in Dedicated mode we can guarantee tail latency by pinning GPUs and using sequence-aware batching. we'll include recommended autoscaling and batch_size profiles in the pilot SOW.
[10:28] Aisha: are there existing exporters or dashboards for the on-prem bundle?
[10:34] Evan: yes — the on-prem package includes a pre-built OTLP collector configuration, Prometheus scrape targets, and Grafana dashboards. we ship them as YAML you can apply. we also provide terraform modules for the VPC bits.
[10:50] Tom: any gotchas with OTLP throughput from many small samples? we worry about collector overload.
[10:58] Priya: best practice: aggregate token events into metrics at the runtime with batching to the collector; use summary/histogram for token latencies rather than raw events. set reasonable batching window (e.g., 200ms) and use gRPC pooling. we can provide a recommended otel-collector config.
[11:23] Dr. Maya: can you demo dynamic sampling?
[11:26] Priya: yes — quick demo (link: redwood/demos/sampling-2025-11-25.mp4). I flip a rule to sample 10%->50% for model.id=rw-llama-13b when suspect_token_rate > 0.01. you see traces increase in Grafana and a matched alert in Prometheus.
[11:48] Liam: after sampling increases do you throttle or backoff to avoid storage blowup?
[11:54] Evan: runtime will apply rate limits per-customer and can spool to local disk for short bursts. the control-plane exposes backpressure signals to the collector so you can cut sampling in the OTLP pipeline as well.
[12:10] Aisha: for our evals we'd like to track jitter per-token across quantization profiles and GPU types. is that feasible?
[12:20] Priya: yes — include labels quant.profile and hw.backend (e.g., a100-v4, h100, onprem-cpu) on metrics. then you can pivot on those in Grafana. we also provide a matrix CSV exporter for bench results.
[12:40] Tom: curious about security — audit logs for telemetry access?
[12:45] Evan: all telemetry access is logged. in Private you control retention and access via your IAM; we emit audit.audit_event metrics and you can forward full audit logs to your SIEM.
[13:00] Dr. Maya: what about multi-tenant isolation — we will run some smaller internal teams and one regulated product that must be siloed.
[13:10] Priya: recommend Dedicated pools with per-tenant namespaces and RBAC. telemetry namespaces will be separate and we can enforce exporter endpoints inside tenants' VPC subnets.
[13:25] Jordan: let's circle back on observability UX — what panels should be in a first-pass dashboard for Sable?
[13:33] Evan: minimal set: 1) token_latency histogram (p50/p95/p99), 2) kv_cache_hit_rate over time, 3) batch_size distribution, 4) cost_per_1k_tokens by model, 5) suspect_token_rate heatmap by model.variant, 6) trace sampling rate and storage usage, 7) trace examples (sampled) linked to logs.
[13:56] Aisha: perfect. Can we add a panel that surfaces top prompts that cause long tail latency?
[14:03] Priya: yes — we have a derived panel that groups request.hash and shows average p95 latency and example prompt (redacted) for privacy.
[14:18] Liam: timeline — we want to pilot in staging with 2 models and 1k rps equivalent for 3 weeks. is that realistic?
[14:27] Jordan: yes — our typical pilot is 2-3 weeks, dedicated small pool, and we run a benchmark harness with your prompt set. we'll include observability config, dashboards, and a runbook.
[14:40] Tom: pricing for that?
[14:43] Jordan: I'll send estimates in the SOW. also options for a host/shared pilot if you want lower cost without full isolation.
[14:56] Dr. Maya: last compliance Q — can telemetry data be redacted automatically? some prompts contain PHI.
[15:06] Priya: we support sanitizer hooks that run before telemetry emission. you can blacklist fields or run regex-based redaction; we also support PII classifiers to auto-redact tokens or mask prompts before storing them. we'll include sanitizer config examples.
[15:22] Speaker 1: (agreement)
